subject: MAP: Load/replay booking and dedicated capacity — CloudMetrics
messages:
From: Evan Ward <evan.ward@cloudmetrics.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kick — load replay window + QPS clarifications

Marissa / Ben / Neha,

Thanks for the call today — we appreciated the clear MAP outline. To lock the load/perf milestone we need to confirm two items from your side so procurement and our infra team can align:

- A recommended replay window (duration and preferred dates) — our peak QPS is ~4,500 for the checkout service across a 6-minute spike. We typically run a 90-minute replay to capture ramp and tail; does Redwood need longer to warm KV cache?
- Guidance on Dedicated capacity sizing or whether we should expect to use a hosted fallback during the test.

We attached our current MAP draft and a small manifest of sample traces. Can you send a short schedule proposal (dates + responsibilities) and a target close date for this milestone so we can update our internal project plan?

Priya (CC) is our infra lead and will coordinate procurement.

Thanks,
Evan

Evan Ward
Senior SRE, CloudMetrics
evan.ward@cloudmetrics.com
(415) 555-0122

Attachment: MAP_CloudMetrics_v0.2.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: replay_dataset_manifest.csv (csv)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ward <evan.ward@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kick — load replay window + QPS clarifications

Evan — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the MAP draft. High level answers below, and I attached an updated MAP with milestone owners and a proposed week-of schedule.

Summary answers:
- Replay window: we recommend a 120-minute window for your profile. That gives us time to: warm KV cache, run two full ramp cycles to validate auto-batching behavior, and run the peak QPS segment twice.
- Dedicated sizing: based on 4,500 peak QPS and the model family you mentioned on the call (redwood-35b-fp16-q4), the safe reserved footprint is 8x A100-80GB equivalent for the replay window to keep latency in SLO. We can present a cost/throughput trade-off matrix if you want smaller reserved + hosted fallback.

Attached: MAP_CloudMetrics_v0.3.xlsx (with milestones), replay_test_plan.md (test procedure).

Proposed milestone & target close:
- Milestone: Load/Traffic replay execution (MAP milestone #3)
- Target close date: 2027-07-01 (complete run + post-run QA report)
- Responsibilities: Redwood: scheduling, test orchestration, monitoring and baseline traces (Ben, Rishi). CloudMetrics: provide signed dataset manifest, validate endpoints, procurement for reserved capacity (Evan/Priya).
- Dependencies: procurement approval for dedicated capacity; isolation VPC peering completed; sample traces validated for PII removal.

Next steps: please confirm whether the week of 2027-06-28 works for the replay window (we suggested June 29 02:00–04:00 UTC in the attached schedule). If procurement needs more lead time we can shift by one week.

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: MAP_CloudMetrics_v0.3.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: replay_test_plan.md (markdown)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ward <evan.ward@cloudmetrics.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kick — load replay window + QPS clarifications

Evan — quick technical note from our side:

- KV warm: 120 minutes is conservative but safe; with a prefix cache we can reduce to 60 minutes if you can provide a trimmed trace that prioritizes hot prefixes.
- Autoscaling & fallback: for the 8x A100 sizing Marissa mentioned, we expect 95th percentile token latency < 220 ms under your stated request mix. If you prefer a hybrid approach we can run the same test with reserved capacity at 6x and let hosted instances handle bursts — we will auto-failover and capture the behavior for the post-run report.

Action items on my side: I will prepare a test orchestration playbook and a short runbook for your SREs to follow during the window. I also need your expected tokenization ratio (avg tokens per request) — if you can share that we will finalize the capacity numbers.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Ward <evan.ward@cloudmetrics.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cloudmetrics.com>, procurement@cloudmetrics.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kick — load replay window + QPS clarifications

Marissa / Ben — appreciate the fast turnaround. A couple of clarifications:

- Tokenization: our checkout service average is 210 tokens per request (includes metadata).
- We can provide a hot-prefix-trimmed trace by EOD tomorrow.
- Procurement: we should be able to approve a reserved footprint but need cost estimate for the 8x A100 configuration (and the hybrid 6x + hosted fallback option). Can you attach a short cost sketch?

Also, June 29 UTC window works for our ops team (Priya confirmed on the call). If Redwood can provide the orchestration playbook then Priya and procurement can finalize the signoff early next week.

Thanks,
Evan
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kick — load replay window + QPS clarifications

Thanks Evan — noted on tokens. Quick engineering commitment and next deliverables from Redwood:

1) By EOD 2027-06-23: orchestration playbook (runbook), and two cost sketches (8x reserved; 6x reserved + hosted fallback).
2) By EOD 2027-06-24: test harness artifact (small container image + invocation script) and a checklist for VPC peering / endpoint readiness.
3) Target: execute replay on 2027-06-29 02:00–04:00 UTC, deliver post-run QA report by 2027-07-01.

If we get the trimmed trace tomorrow we will run a quick local validation and tighten the reservation if it looks like hot-prefix coverage is high.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
